title: ArgumentFormatter doesn't pretty-print rank-1 variable-bound arrays correctly

labels.name: Bug
labels.description: A fault in an existing feature

labels.name: help wanted
labels.description: A community-provided PR would be welcomed

labels.name: good first issue
labels.description: This may be a good issue for a first-time contributor

body:
## Summary

`ArgumentFormatter` does not pretty-print rank-1 variable-bound arrays correctly. It prints `int[]` when it should instead print `int[*]`.

## Repro

In the file __ArgumentFormatterTests.cs__, take this theory data:

https://github.com/xunit/xunit/blob/c27a91f8cbcee37cb45699a3a81287bca225e876/src/xunit.v3.assert.tests/Asserts/Sdk/ArgumentFormatterTests.cs#L176-L189

And insert this test case into it:

```cs
{ typeof(int).MakeArrayType(1), "typeof(int[*])" },
```

Then run __build.cmd__ and you will observe the failure when the unit tests run.

```txt
xUnit.net v3 In-Process Runner v0.1.1-pre.30-dev+c27a91f8cb (64-bit .NET Core 3.1.25)
  Discovering: xunit.v3.assert.tests (method display = ClassAndMethod, method display options = None)
  Discovered:  xunit.v3.assert.tests (found 826 test cases)
  Starting:    xunit.v3.assert.tests (parallel test collections = on, max threads = unlimited)
    ArgumentFormatterTests+SimpleValues.TypeValue(type: typeof(int[]), expected: "typeof(int[*])") [FAIL]
      Assert.Equal() Failure
                           ↓ (pos 11)
      Expected: typeof(int[*])
      Actual:   typeof(int[])
                           ↑ (pos 11)
      Stack Trace:
        C:\xunit\src\xunit.v3.assert.tests\Asserts\Sdk\ArgumentFormatterTests.cs(197,0): at ArgumentFormatterTests.SimpleValues.TypeValue(Type type, String expected)
  Finished:    xunit.v3.assert.tests
=== TEST EXECUTION SUMMARY ===
   xunit.v3.assert.tests  Total: 883, Errors: 0, Failed: 1, Skipped: 0, Time: 0.253s
```

## Sample fix

The issue is in these lines in __ArgumentFormatter.cs__.

https://github.com/xunit/assert.xunit/blob/43e3e208a597bc1a4c77f2665f39f98e7401c157/Sdk/ArgumentFormatter.cs#L310-L320

They should have a call to [`Type.IsSZArray`](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.type.isszarray), as shown below.

```cs
if (typeInfo.IsSZArray)
{
	arraySuffix += "[]";
}
else
{
	var rank = typeInfo.GetArrayRank();
	if (rank == 1)
	{
		arraySuffix += "[*]";
	}
	else
	{
		arraySuffix += $"[{new string(',', rank - 1)}]";
	}
}
```

This can also be implemented as an extension method to work downlevel.

```cs
public static bool IsSzArrayType(this Type type)
{
#if NETCOREAPP2_0_OR_GREATER
    // framework built-in function
    return type.IsSZArray;
#else
    // bounce through a few layers of indirection to detect this
    return type.IsArray && type == type.GetElementType().MakeArrayType();
#endif
}
```

## Discussion

In .NET, there are actually __three__ ways to represent arrays:

* `int[]`, which is a standard single-dimensional, zero-indexed array ("SZ array")
* `int[,,,]`, which is a multi-dimensional array (not necessarily zero-indexed)
* `int[*]`, which is a single-dimensional array (not necessarily zero-indexed)

The last two are also called _variable-bound arrays_, and the rank-1 syntax of `[*]` has an asterisk to disambiguate it from the standard `[]` SZ array syntax.

This is fairly easy to see in PowerShell as well:

```txt
❯ [int].MakeArrayType().Name
Int32[]

❯ [int].MakeArrayType(1).Name
Int32[*]

❯ [int].MakeArrayType(2).Name
Int32[,]

# Also shows that the runtime considers int[] and int[*] truly different, incompatible types
❯ [int].MakeArrayType().Equals([int].MakeArrayType(1))
False
```
